name: Filipino Pork Sinigang with Rice

components.name: Pork Sinigang

ingredients.name: Boneless pork shoulder, cut in chunks

steps: Add 1800 ml water, diced onion and half the tomatoes to a heavy pot. Bring to a simmer.
Add pork shoulder, skim foam and cook gently until almost tender, around 60 minutes depending on chunk size.
Stir tamarind paste into a little hot broth until smooth; return to pot, then add radish and eggplant.
After a few minutes, add long beans, okra, chilli and remaining tomatoes. Cook until tender but still holding their shape.
Finish with chopped water spinach, fish sauce and black pepper; turn off heat once greens are wilted.
Portion pork, broth, vegetables and rice consistently; label prominently NON-HALAL / CONTAINS PORK.

components.name: Jasmine Rice
steps: Rinse rice and cook in a covered pot with 390 ml water; rest before portioning.

notes: Draft — needs Mirna review: not kitchen-tested yet; macros and cooked yields are estimates.

CONTAINS PORK; NOT HALAL. Uses pork shoulder instead of source belly, a cut the source explicitly allows, and adds rice. Uses pre-made tamarind puree to avoid boiling whole fruit; source uses young tamarind.
Storing & reheating: Freeze pork and sour broth; leafy greens and okra lose texture. Fresh greens may be added during reheating.
Keeps 3–4 days in the fridge (≤4°C); refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers, freeze portions for later in the week, and reheat to at least 74°C.
